title: Closing the Question on the Continuation of Turn-of-the-Month Effects: Evidence from the S&P 500 Index Futures Contract
one_line: The classic turn-of-the-month effect (last trading day + first three days of the month) disappeared from S&P 500 futures and the spot index after 1990.

findings.statement: Turn-of-the-month effects in S&P 500 futures disappear after 1990; same for the spot index.
findings.evidence: Atlanta Fed WP 2000-11; TOTM = last trading day + next three trading days.

findings.statement: Calendar patterns are tied to market microstructure and can change without notice.

why.pattern: Institutional constraint / payment cycles (classic TOTM) — weakened as retail moved to mutual funds.
why.mechanism: Authors conjecture the shift from direct stock buying to mutual funds changed month-end cash flows.
why.what_would_kill_it: Already reported dead post-1990 in futures (pre-2000 data).

reported_results.headline: TOTM effect gone after 1990 in S&P futures.

tradable_edge: No new strategy — a warning for month_end_rebalance_es: the naive TOTM window failed in futures after 1990, so any month-end spec needs the settlement-timed version (Dash for Cash) and must beat this naive window as a baseline.
angles: Use the naive TOTM window (T-1 to T+3) as a required baseline in month-end tests
data_fit: ES 1-min (ETH + RTH) Dec 2013 → Sep 2026 in clean_ES_master.parquet; NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026. 2024+ is protected in the backtest project.
caveats: Abstract-level only; no return figures recorded.
